newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain probe finds ETA suspect was not tortured.
newsitem.headline: Spain probe finds ETA suspect was not tortured.

text.p: The Spanish government denied allegations that an ETA suspect was tortured by police and said he had admitted to shooting and killing two men.

It ordered an inquiry after defence lawyers said Fernando Elejalde maintained he was beaten while in police custody, suffering four crushed vertebrae, a ruptured kidney, a perforated eardrum and widespread bruising.

"The report concludes that Elejalde was not tortured or maltreated after his detention and that he sustained the injuries after being hit by a car and during a violent arrest," the Interior Ministry told Reuters late on Sunday.
Police arrested Elejalde, 29, after a gun battle on the streets of the Basque city of San Sebastian as he ran from the scene of the killing of prison psychologist Javier Garcia Elosegui.
He was taken to hospital from police cells semi-conscious and in serious condition on Thursday, two days after his arrest.
The government said he told a Supreme Court judge during an interrogation at his hospital bedside on Saturday that he had taken part in two fatal shootings.
"He has admitted to the killing of Elosegui as well as a bicycle vendor earlier this year," the Interior Ministry said.

A bicycle salesman was shot in the head and killed in San Sebastian in January in an attack blamed by the government on ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom). Press reports said ETA might have suspected the vendor of turning in one of its activists.

Defence lawyers said Elejalde claimed he had been arrested peacefully. "He told us that the blows he received started when he arrived at the police station and that none of the injuries were a result of the arrest," said lawyer Ainhoa Baigliot.

She said Elejalde, who was taken to an emergency clinic two hours after his arrest, reported that police continued to beat him on Wednesday and Thursday. "They put him on his knees and hit him with an unknown instrument," she said.

But the Interior Ministry said its inquiry found that the injuries reported on Tuesday "clearly coincided" with those reported two days later, showing that he was hurt during the arrest and not by torture.
"The reason why he was not taken to the hospital again until Thursday was that he simply did not tell police he was in pain," it said.
A Supreme Court judge has ruled that Elejalde should be held without bail and court sources said he would be transferred to a prison as soon as he was well enough.
Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja was due to give a detailed explanation of the inquiry's findings to parliament on Monday.

He had to explain to parliament last week what happened to a suspected ETA member who was found hanged in his prison cell with his feet and hands tied, facts that were not immediately released by the government.
Officials said it was suicide, but Basque nationalists accused the government of a cover up and said it was "difficult to imagine" how someone could hang themselves while bound.
